introduction: A process-health check can remain green while users cannot list tasks. Observability begins with a question about user behavior and adds enough measurement to answer it. You will instrument the familiar API and distinguish process health, dependency readiness and a meaningful synthetic request.

To keep the stack small, this lesson uses the existing local Compose Taskboard as a separate telemetry sandbox, with its own existing Compose database. It does not change the Kubernetes GitOps deployment. All dashboards bind to127.0.0.1; metrics are not a public endpoint.
prerequisites: Ubuntu 24.04 Bash in WSL2 or a disposable Linux VM; Docker is running. Use the same terminal unless a step names a second terminal.
Taskboard at ~/dev-opps-lab/app/taskboard with its generated .env and Compose setup from earlier lessons. Local ports8000/9090/3000 free. Stop an earlier Compose app before rebuilding its image.

concepts.title: Counters, rates and histograms
paragraphs: A counter accumulates events; rate over a time window estimates events per second and handles resets. An error ratio divides bad events by eligible events over the same window. A histogram counts observations in cumulative duration buckets; its sum/count supports a mean while bucket ratios support threshold SLOs.
concepts.example: 100successful health checks can hide10failed task-list requests; choose endpoint eligibility explicitly.
concepts.judgment: A panel is useful when it changes a decision. Show request rate, error fraction, latency and saturation rather than collecting every available metric.

concepts.title: Cardinality and the observer boundary
paragraphs: Each distinct label combination creates another series. Route templates such as /tasks/{task_id} stay bounded; actual IDs, raw URLs, user IDs and tokens do not. The instrumentation below labels the matched template and uses <unmatched> for unknown routes.

Prometheus scrapes from outside the application process. A separate synthetic request validates a response contract. Gatus embodies that same distinction: status alone is weaker than status plus expected body and latency.
concepts.example: A200response with no items field violates the list contract even if its status is green.
concepts.judgment: Keep application authentication checks, synthetic-monitor credentials and telemetry access scoped independently.

steps.title: Add explicit metrics instrumentation
steps.purpose: Create a small wrapper without changing domain logic.

commands.code:
cd "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/app/taskboard"
mkdir -p observability
cat > reference/metrics.py <<'PY'
import time
from fastapi import Response
from prometheus_client import Counter, Histogram, generate_latest, CONTENT_TYPE_LATEST
from reference.stage07 import app
requests = Counter("taskboard_http_requests_total", "Completed HTTP requests", ["method", "route", "status"])
duration = Histogram("taskboard_http_duration_seconds", "HTTP response duration", ["method", "route"], buckets=[.005,.01,.025,.05,.1,.25,.5,1,2,5])
@app.middleware("http")
async def measure(request, call_next):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    response = await call_next(request)
    if request.url.path != "/metrics":
        route = getattr(request.scope.get("route"), "path", "<unmatched>")
        requests.labels(request.method, route, str(response.status_code)).inc()
        duration.labels(request.method, route).observe(time.perf_counter()-started)
    return response
@app.get("/metrics", include_in_schema=False)
async def metrics():
    return Response(generate_latest(), media_type=CONTENT_TYPE_LATEST)
PY
cat > Dockerfile.metrics <<'DOCKER'
FROM devopps-taskboard:w25
USER root
RUN python -m pip install --no-cache-dir prometheus-client==0.22.1
COPY reference/metrics.py /app/reference/metrics.py
USER 10001:10001
DOCKER
docker build -f Dockerfile.metrics -t devopps-taskboard:metrics .
explain: The heredoc writes a wrapper around stage07. Counter counts completed responses by bounded method/route/status; Histogram records seconds with explicit buckets. /metrics exposes Prometheus text and is excluded from its own request count.

The derived Dockerfile adds only the pinned metrics dependency and wrapper to the familiar runtime image, then returns to UID10001. -f selects that Dockerfile. This single-process example needs additional multiprocess configuration if you later run multiple Uvicorn workers.
commands.expected: New image builds; domain/API tests remain applicable.
commands.troubleshoot: If the base tag is absent, rebuild week25 runtime first. Do not install packages interactively into a running container and call that reproducible.

steps.title: Start a single metrics stack
steps.purpose: Resolve official component versions once and retain them locally.

commands.code:
PROMETHEUS_TAG=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/prometheus/prometheus/releases/latest | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["tag_name"])')
GRAFANA_TAG=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/grafana/grafana/releases/latest | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["tag_name"].removeprefix("v"))')
GRAFANA_PASSWORD=$(python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(24))')
printf 'PROMETHEUS_TAG=%s
GRAFANA_TAG=%s
GRAFANA_PASSWORD=%s
' "$PROMETHEUS_TAG" "$GRAFANA_TAG" "$GRAFANA_PASSWORD" > observability/local.env
chmod 600 observability/local.env
printf "\nobservability/local.env\n" >> .gitignore
set -a
. observability/local.env
set +a
cat > observability/prometheus.yml <<'YAML'
global:
  scrape_interval: 5s
scrape_configs:
- job_name: taskboard
  static_configs:
  - targets: ['app:8000']
YAML
cat > observability/datasource.yml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: 1
datasources:
- name: Taskboard
  uid: taskboard-prom
  type: prometheus
  access: proxy
  url: http://prometheus:9090
  isDefault: true
YAML
cat > observability.yaml <<'YAML'
services:
  app:
    image: devopps-taskboard:metrics
    command: [python, -m, uvicorn, 'reference.metrics:app', --host, 0.0.0.0, --port, '8000', --no-access-log]
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:${PROMETHEUS_TAG}
    command: [--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml, --storage.tsdb.retention.time=24h]
    volumes: ['./observability/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro']
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:9090:9090']
    networks: [backend]
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:${GRAFANA_TAG}
    environment:
      GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${GRAFANA_PASSWORD}
      GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP: 'false'
    volumes:
    - './observability/datasource.yml:/etc/grafana/provisioning/datasources/lab.yml:ro'
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:3000:3000']
    networks: [backend]
YAML
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f observability.yaml up -d db migrate app prometheus grafana
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/metrics
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9090/-/ready
explain: Official GitHub release responses supply concrete image versions. Store them with the random local Grafana password in a600-permission file; add observability/local.env to .gitignore before staging anything. set -a exports assignments loaded from this locally generated file; set +a ends automatic exporting.

Prometheus scrapes app:8000 every5seconds and retains24hours. Grafana's provisioned datasource uses the internal service address. The overlay changes only app image/command and adds the two services; ports are loopback-only. up starts the Compose dependency chain, including migrations.
curl checks metrics exposition and Prometheus readiness independently. Open http://127.0.0.1:3000 and log in as admin with the locally generated password; never commit or share it.
The .gitignore entry prevents the local Grafana credential file from being staged; it does not remove a secret already committed, which would require rotation and history review.
commands.expected: Metrics text includes taskboard_http_requests_total after traffic; Prometheus ready endpoint succeeds.
commands.troubleshoot: If up fails because a version variable is absent, reload observability/local.env in this terminal. Check Prometheus Targets for scrape errors rather than treating an empty graph as zero failures.

steps.checkpoint: In Grafana create four Time series panels using the queries below; save the dashboard and export its JSON into observability/dashboard.json.

steps.title: Build decision-oriented panels and a synthetic check
steps.purpose: Use exact queries and validate the list contract.

explain: These are PromQL expressions for Grafana query editors, not shell commands. Use panel titles Requests per second, Server-error fraction, Task-list p95 seconds and Resident memory bytes.

rate uses a1-minute window; the denominator guard avoids divide-by-zero but an idle period is still no evidence of success. histogram_quantile estimates p95 from buckets; resident memory shows one saturation clue, not a total capacity verdict.
commands.expected: Panels populate after several scrapes and requests.
commands.troubleshoot: Check label spelling and target health first; a missing series differs from a zero-valued sample.

commands.code:
set -a
. .env
set +a
export LAB_ALICE_TOKEN
python3 - <<'PY'
import json,os,time,urllib.request
start=time.perf_counter()
r=urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8000/tasks',headers={'Authorization':'Bearer '+os.environ['LAB_ALICE_TOKEN']})
with urllib.request.urlopen(r,timeout=2) as response:
 body=json.load(response)
 assert response.status==200 and isinstance(body.get('items'),list), 'List contract failed'
assert time.perf_counter()-start < 2, 'Latency threshold failed'
print('SYNTHETIC_PASS')
PY
explain: Load only the locally generated .env values; the Python script checks authenticated200, an items array and a chosen2-second lab bound. Assertions make bad data visible even when status200.
commands.troubleshoot: A401means the monitor identity is wrong; a503can be dependency failure. Preserve the distinction in the runbook.

steps.checkpoint: State the question and next action for every panel; record the synthetic location and what it cannot see.

failure.title: The process lives while task access fails
failure.boundary: Stop only the Compose lab database; the Kubernetes database is separate.

inject.code: docker compose -f compose.yaml -f observability.yaml stop db
explain: Stop the scoped dependency while leaving the app process running.
inject.expected: /livez stays200; /readyz and authenticated task requests fail.
inject.troubleshoot: If the app itself exits, inspect its logs and separate that symptom from the intended dependency fault.

explain: -o discards bodies while -w prints status; the authorized request measures user behavior, not merely process existence.
investigate.troubleshoot: If tasks401 check the token; do not count unauthorized monitor configuration as database failure.

explanation: The app is capable of executing its health handler but its useful dependency is unavailable. A process-only monitor misses the incident.

recover.code: docker compose -f compose.yaml -f observability.yaml start db
explain: Restart the same database with its retained volume.
recover.troubleshoot: Wait for pg_isready rather than repeatedly restarting the app.

explain: Verify the user endpoint after recovery.
verification.troubleshoot: Re-run the full synthetic assertion, not only this status check.

questions.prompt: Why can total error ratio hide a broken endpoint?
questions.answer: Frequent healthy health checks can dominate the denominator. Define eligible user routes and inspect important route-specific symptoms.

questions.prompt: Why not label metrics with a task ID?
questions.hint: How many series after a year?
questions.answer: Each new ID adds distinct series and memory/storage cost. Use route templates; keep specific IDs in carefully scoped diagnostic events when necessary.
No eligible requests means no request-based evidence. Synthetic coverage can provide another signal, but its definition must remain separate.

exercise.brief: Improve one dashboard panel and synthetic contract.
acceptance: Wrong body with200would fail the check
hints: Separate process, dependency and user-path checks.
solution: Use the exact/task route denominator, document the2-second chosen lab threshold, and add a response-shape assertion. Record a database outage and recovery in the same dashboard window.

explain: Keep the recovered stack for week34. Stop it with the same compose files and down when ending the lab; omit -v to retain deliberate database data.
cleanup.expected: Only intended local services are running.
cleanup.troubleshoot: Avoid docker system prune; it affects unrelated projects.

repoConnections.principle: Check the contract, not merely status.
repoConnections.application: The independent authenticated list check validates both status and body; the database fault proves why process health is weaker.

repoConnections.principle: Use signals to answer a question.
repoConnections.application: This lesson starts with aggregate symptoms; the next adds request traces without installing a second full observability suite.

notes: Instrumentation and configuration are provided in full; container execution was not available during authoring.
title: Measure the user experience
outcome: Instrument useful metrics and create a small actionable dashboard.
